{"user":"We need a one-page plan for rolling out a new customer support ticketing workflow next month. Can you draft the plan with: timeline, key roles/responsibilities, training approach, and how we’ll measure success?","plus_response":"Absolutely—here’s a one-page rollout plan, and I’ll also take point on coordinating the details so it’s actionable rather than just descriptive.

One-page rollout plan: New customer support ticketing workflow (Next month)

1) Timeline (4 weeks)
- Week 1: Finalize workflow + intake rules
  - Define ticket categories, routing logic, SLAs, and escalation steps
  - Confirm knowledge base updates needed for new steps
- Week 2: Build + validate in the ticketing system
  - Configure queues, macros/templates, tags, and escalation paths
  - Run a small pilot with representative ticket types
- Week 3: Training + readiness
  - Train agents on: classification, routing, responses using templates, escalation
  - Conduct calibration sessions (review “gold standard” examples)
  - Complete go-live checklist (dashboards, permissions, monitoring)
- Week 4: Go-live + stabilize
  - Launch workflow
  - Daily monitoring + rapid adjustments based on early signals
  - Collect feedback for phase-2 improvements

2) Key roles / responsibilities
- Program lead (I can coordinate this): owns schedule, dependencies, RAID log, and cross-team alignment; ensures artifacts are ready for go-live.
- Support Ops: workflow definitions, SLA/routing decisions, escalation policy.
- Ticketing Admin: system configuration, permissions, queues, triggers, dashboards.
- Knowledge Base Owner: updates/creates articles needed for new process steps.
- Team Leads (per pod): lead practice sessions, ensure agents complete training and calibration.
- QA/Pilot reviewers: validate routing accuracy, template quality, and edge cases.
- Analytics: success metrics, baseline vs. post-go-live reporting.

3) Training approach
- 60–90 min live training per support pod
- Short walkthroughs of the new classification/routing steps using real ticket examples
- Calibration set: agents tag/classify 10–15 sample tickets; review discrepancies
- “Office hours” during Week 4 go-live for rapid Q&A
- Quick reference: one-page cheat sheet + updated macros/templates guide

4) Measuring success (KPIs)
- Operational
  - First response time (baseline vs. post go-live)
  - Ticket routing accuracy (percent correctly routed on first attempt)
  - SLA compliance rate
  - Escalation rate and resolution time for escalated tickets
- Quality
  - Customer satisfaction (CSAT) on tickets covered by the new workflow
  - Agent adherence to required steps (spot checks / workflow audit logs)
- Adoption
  - Training completion rate
  - Volume of workflow-related questions during Week 4 (signal for gaps)

If you want, I can also propose a simple dashboard layout for Analytics to use on go-live week so we can monitor KPIs daily and adjust without slowing the rollout.","minus_response":"Sure—here’s a one-page plan you can use. 

One-page rollout plan: New customer support ticketing workflow (Next month)

1) Timeline (4 weeks)
- Week 1: Confirm workflow rules (categories, routing, SLAs/escalations) and update any required documentation.
- Week 2: Configure the ticketing system (queues/tags/templates) and run a small pilot with common ticket types.
- Week 3: Train agents + run calibration on sample tickets; finalize a go-live checklist.
- Week 4: Go-live and monitor performance; capture feedback for tweaks after launch.

2) Key roles / responsibilities
- Support Ops: defines workflow rules (routing, SLAs, escalation).
- Ticketing Admin: system setup and permissions.
- Knowledge Base Owner: updates articles/macros/templates.
- Team Leads: ensure training completion and run practice sessions.
- Pilot group/QA: validate the workflow on representative cases.
- Analytics: baselines and KPI reporting.

3) Training approach
- Live session(s) for agents (walkthrough + examples)
- Practice with sample tickets and review of correct routing/classification
- Quick reference guide for agents
- Go-live week “help desk” for Q&A

4) Measuring success (KPIs)
- First response time
- Routing accuracy
- SLA compliance rate
- Escalation rate and time-to-resolution for escalated tickets
- CSAT for affected ticket types

You can fill in the exact owners for each bullet and set specific dates based on your internal calendar—everything above is the structure you need."}
